item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
315
ABPZ20 KNHC 010532
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 PM PDT Mon Aug 31 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Karina, located well west-southwest of the southern tip of the Baja
California Peninsula, and on Tropical Storm Lowell, located well
southeast of the Hawaiian Islands.

Well Offshore of Southwestern Mexico (EP95):
Satellite-derived wind data indicate that a tropical storm appears
to be forming with an area of low pressure located about 500 miles
south-southwest of Manzanillo, Mexico. Advisories on this system
will likely be initiated on early Tuesday. The system is moving
northwestward around 10 mph. For more information, including storm
warnings, please see the High Seas forecast issued by the National
Weather Service.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...high...near 100 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...near 100 percent.

&&
High Seas Forecasts issued by the National Weather Service
can be found under AWIPS header NFDHSFEPI, WMO header FZPN02
KWBC, and on the web at ocean.weather.gov/shtml/NFDHSFEPI.php

$$
Forecaster Pasch

...KARINA SLIGHTLY STRONGER...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 1100 PM HST...0900 UTC...INFORMATION
-----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...18.0N 127.9W
ABOUT 1210 MI...1950 KM WSW OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...140 MPH...220 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...WNW OR 285 DEGREES AT 10 MPH...17 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...945 MB...27.91 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 1100 PM HST (0900 UTC), the center of Hurricane Karina was
located near latitude 18.0 North, longitude 127.9 West.  Karina is
moving toward the west-northwest near 10 mph (17 km/h) and this
general motion is expected to continue for the next few days.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 140 mph (220 km/h) with higher
gusts.  Karina is a category 4 hurricane on the Saffir-Simpson
Hurricane Wind Scale.  Fluctuations in intensity are possible 
through Tuesday morning followed by a gradual weakening trend 
beginning by late Tuesday.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 30 miles (45 km) from the
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 115 miles
(185 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 945 mb (27.91 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
SURF: Swells generated by Karina will affect portions of the coast
of southwest Mexico and the Baja California Peninsula for the next
couple of days and will likely spread northward to southern
California through midweek.  These swells are likely to cause
life-threatening surf and rip current conditions. Please consult
products from your local weather office. A depiction of rip current
risk for the United States can be found at:
hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep1.shtml?ripCurrents
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 500 AM HST.
 
$$
Forecaster Pasch

item.title: Hurricane Karina Forecast Discussion Number 20
item.description:
Issued at 1100 PM HST Mon Aug 31 2026 
000
WTPZ41 KNHC 010836
TCDEP1
 
Hurricane Karina Discussion Number  20
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP112026
1100 PM HST Mon Aug 31 2026

Karina is maintaining a well-defined eye surrounded by very deep 
convection with cloud tops to -80 deg C or even colder.  Subjective 
Dvorak estimates indicate that the hurricane is maintaining its 
intensity.  In fact, the objective satellite consensus intensity 
estimate, SATCON, from UW-CIMSS suggests that Karina has become 
slightly stronger with an estimated maximum wind speed near 120 kt 
for this advisory.  There is not much evidence of concentric 
eyewalls at this time, and Karina still has some potential to become 
an annular hurricane.

The estimated motion continues to be west-northwestward, or    
285/9 kt.  A narrow mid-tropospheric subtropical ridge to the north 
of Karina should keep the system on a west-northwestward to westward 
track at about the same forward speed through 72 hours or so.  By 
days 4-5 a weak mid-level low to the north of the Hawaiian Islands 
should induce a slightly more northwestward motion.  The official 
track forecast is similar to the previous one, and is close to the 
simple model consensus.  The corrected consensus is a little north 
of the NHC track in the latter part of the forecast period.

Karina is likely to remain over marginally warm ocean waters with 
low vertical wind shear for the next couple of days.  This should 
keep the system as a major hurricane through the next 36 hours or 
so.  Although a slightly drier low- to mid-level air mass and 
gradually cooling SSTs should result in slow weakening, Karina 
could maintain its intensity more than expected if it takes on an 
annular structure.  The official intensity forecast is similar to 
the model consensus and on the high side of the guidance envelope.

item.title: Tropical Storm Marie Forecast Discussion Number 1
item.description:
Issued at 200 AM MST Tue Sep 01 2026 
658 
WTPZ43 KNHC 010840
TCDEP3
 
Tropical Storm Marie Discussion Number   1
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP132026
200 AM MST Tue Sep 01 2026
 
Satellite imagery indicates that the deep convection associated with 
the disturbance offshore of southwestern Mexico has become better 
organized over the past several hours. A 0327 UTC ASCAT-B pass 
showed a well-defined circulation and peak winds of around 40 kt in 
the southeastern quadrant. The scatterometer data also indicated 
that the tropical-storm-force wind field is confined primarily to 
the southern semicircle of the circulation. A subjective Dvorak 
classification from TAFB was T2.5/35 kt. Based on these data, 
advisories are being initiated on Tropical Storm Marie with an 
initial intensity of 40 kt.

Marie is moving northwestward, or 315/8 kt. The subtropical ridge 
extending westward from northern Mexico should steer Marie 
northwestward during the next several days. The ridge is forecast to 
gradually weaken as a broad upper-level trough deepens along the 
U.S. West Coast, which should also result in some decrease in the 
cyclone's forward speed. By days 4 and 5, the upper trough is 
forecast to begin filling while the mid- to upper-level ridge builds 
to the north of Marie, causing the cyclone to gradually turn toward 
the west-northwest. The track guidance remains tightly clustered 
through about day 3, but there is increasing cross-track spread 
thereafter, with some models maintaining a more northward trajectory 
and others showing a sharper west-northwestward turn. The NHC track 
forecast favors the west-northwestward turn shown by the multi-model 
consensus (HCCA) and the Google DeepMind ensemble mean, but 
confidence is lower near the end of the forecast period due to the 
increasing guidance spread.

Environmental conditions appear favorable for Marie to steadily 
strengthen during the next few days. The cyclone is forecast to 
remain over warm waters and within an environment of low vertical 
wind shear and sufficient mid-level moisture. These conditions 
should allow Marie to become a hurricane in a couple of days, with 
additional strengthening forecast thereafter. By days 4 and 5, 
however, Marie is forecast to encounter a progressively drier 
environment while moving over gradually decreasing sea surface 
temperatures. These less favorable conditions should bring an end to 
the strengthening trend and result in gradual weakening by the end 
of the forecast period. The NHC intensity forecast shows Marie 
reaching a peak intensity of around 80 kt in about 3 days, and lies 
near the middle of the intensity guidance envelope.
